signals.SIGHUP: The terminal closed; by convention, a daemon then reloads its configuration (nginx -s reload).
signals.SIGINT: Ctrl+C: interrupt the program in the foreground.
signals.SIGQUIT: Ctrl+\: quit leaving a core dump; the JVM answers it with a thread dump.
signals.SIGTSTP: Ctrl+Z: suspend the program in the foreground; fg or bg resumes it.
signals.SIGTTIN: A background program tried to read from the terminal.
signals.SIGTTOU: A background program tried to write to the terminal, when stty tostop forbids it.
signals.SIGWINCH: The terminal was resized: vim, less or htop redraw.
signals.SIGINFO: Ctrl+T on macOS and the BSDs: the program says how far it got (dd, cp); Linux has none.
signals.SIGTERM: What kill sends with no option: ask politely to stop, which the program may prepare for; docker stop and systemd start with it.
signals.SIGKILL: kill -9: kill with no appeal; no cleanup, no last write.
signals.SIGSTOP: Suspend with no appeal; SIGTSTP's counterpart to SIGKILL.
signals.SIGCONT: Resume a suspended program; what fg and bg do.
signals.SIGABRT: abort(): the program stops itself, an assertion failed.
signals.SIGSEGV: Segmentation fault: access to memory that is not its own.
signals.SIGBUS: Bus error: a misaligned access, or one to a truncated mapped file.
signals.SIGFPE: Arithmetic error: an integer division by zero, most often.
signals.SIGILL: Illegal instruction: a binary built for another processor, for instance.
signals.SIGSYS: A system call refused, by a seccomp filter for instance.
signals.SIGSTKFLT: A coprocessor stack fault; Linux defines it and no longer uses it.
signals.SIGALRM: The timer of alarm() or setitimer() expired.
signals.SIGVTALRM: The timer of the CPU time spent in the program expired.
signals.SIGPROF: The profiling timer expired; profilers sample with it.
signals.SIGXCPU: The CPU time limit (ulimit -t) was exceeded.
signals.SIGXFSZ: The file size limit (ulimit -f) was exceeded.
signals.SIGCHLD: A child process stopped or ended; the parent collects it with wait().
signals.SIGPIPE: A write to a pipe or a socket nobody reads any more: that is how head stops the program before it.
signals.SIGURG: Urgent data arrived on a socket.
signals.SIGIO: I/O is possible on a watched descriptor; also called SIGPOLL.
signals.SIGPWR: A power failure reported by the UPS.
signals.SIGUSR1: Free for the application: reopen the logs, dump a state.
signals.SIGUSR2: Free for the application: reload without downtime, change the log level.
signals.SIGRTMIN: The real-time signals, free for the application, queued rather than merged.
